lines.line: Papa says I'm too friendly with strangers, but you seem all right.
Is there anything I can help you with?
Maybe you can help me.
What do you need?
Of course.
It's all in this note.
Yes, sera?
I don't know what you overheard, but the Riverwood Trader is still open. Feel free to shop.
What happened here?
Uh yeah, we did have a bit of a... a break-in. But we still have plenty to sell. Robbers were only after one thing.
An ornament, solid gold. In the shape of a dragon's claw.
I could help you get the claw back.
You could? I've got some coin coming in from my last shipment. It's yours if you bring my claw back.
Faendal thinks he can woo Camilla Valerius away from me. She's already mine, I keep telling him.
You and Faendal both like the same girl?
Camilla Valerius knows I'm the best man in Riverwood. That elf is kidding himself if he thinks she would choose him over me.
I've seen him sneaking over to the Riverwood Trader to speak with her when I'm not around. He's wasting his time.
He sounds persistent.
You may be right. Camilla may see Faendal as little more than a friend, but why take chances?
Here. Give Camilla this letter. It's full of venomous nonsense. Tell her it's from Faendal.
Whoa, hold on a minute.  I'm staying out of this.
Then what are you wasting my time for?
You look like a traveler. Someone that has seen far away places and heard new stories.
You and Faendal both like the same girl?
Camilla Valerius knows I'm the best man in Riverwood. That elf is kidding himself if he thinks she would choose him over me.
I've seen him sneaking over to the Riverwood Trader to speak with her when I'm not around. He's wasting his time.
Yes. Two people spending time together never blossoms into courtship.
Is that sarcasm? I've heard better wisecracks from Orgnar.
Still, you have a point. Camilla letting Faendal visit her isn't a good thing for me.
Here, let me give you a particularly venomous letter. Say it's from Faendal. That should get Camilla to stop inviting the elf over.
Sure, why not?  This ought to be amusing.
That letter ought to convince Camilla to never speak to Faendal ever again.
Riverwood's agreeable enough, I suppose. For a Nord village.
Sven wanted me to deliver this letter to Camilla, saying it was from you.
What is that blowhard up to now?
So, he thinks he can turn Camilla against me? Two can play at this.
Here. Give this letter to Camilla and tell her it's from Sven. Let's see what she thinks of him after reading that.
Mara bless you for agreeing to help us.
I have a letter for you, from Sven. (Lie)
Another poem, I bet. He does know how to make a girl blush.
What's this? If that oaf thinks all I'm going to do is stay in that filthy house of his and clean, I'll...
You can tell Sven that he already has a mother. I'm not speaking to him anymore.
There's beauty here unmatched in all of Skyrim, to be sure.
I don't think Camilla will be spending any more time with Sven.
I appreciate your help. Please, take this. Some gold I've saved up from working at the mill.
You're that visitor, been pokin' around.
I'd like to rent a room. (10 gold)
Sure thing. It's yours for a day.
Helgen... destroyed by a dragon. Hard to believe, isn't it?
What can you tell me about Riverwood?
It's my mill. Some folks thinks it's my town, too, but it ain't. The Jarl in Whiterun owns the land and the town. I just pay the taxes.
Ain't every day we get visitors in Riverwood.
What can you tell me about Riverwood?
Gerdur's family first settled here as woodcutters a few generations ago.
She and Hod run the mill. I make a decent living sharpening axes and fixing the sawmill.
Greetings stranger, the name's Hjoromir, and I'm at your service.
Let me know if there's anything I can help you with.  Perhaps you need your boots shined, or your tunic washed, or need a letter delivered?
Unfortunately lad, I need no such services.
Well, maybe you need someone to chop you some firewood.  Or brew you an alchemy potion.  I think I have a recipe lying around somewhere...
You're really bad at this.
Maybe. Or maybe I just need the right teacher.  You seem well traveled.
Are you in need of an apprentice?  I'll cook and clean, and can set traps to catch game.
I'll consider it.
R-really?  I'll do everything you ask, just say the word!
You're fairly young for someone living out on his own.
I'm of age, and a man grown.  I can grow whiskers on my cheeks just like any old Nord.
People treat me differently because of my station, but they still respect me as a man.  Which is more than I can say for my father.
The last time I saw the old toad all he did was bark orders and gripe.  He complained my pheasant roast was overcooked.
He nearly slapped me when I poured his beer and left a less than frothy head, and then he berated me the entire time I cleared the table.
I'm sorry. That must be difficult for you.
Yeah, but at least when he's eating he keeps his mouth shut.  The worst part is afterward, when he starts spouting racist nonsense.
Elves poisoning our food. Elves stealing our children. And don't tell him there's a difference between the Elven races, let alone Altmer and Thalmor.
They're all Thalmor maggots to him.  Listening to the old man makes me ashamed to call myself a Nord.
What about your mother?
Ah, my mother is a kind woman.  She always compliments me on my meals, and tells me how proud she is to have me for a son.
That's it's own dilemma.  When even I can tell my potage has no flavor, it's tough to appreciate the kindness of her words.
While lies of deceit are born as spiders and die as flies, white lies can wilt like a rose and leave nothing but thorns.
That's enough about your family.
And I've had enough of talking about them, as it were.  At least, to anyone who isn't a patron.
Do you have a job in town?
If you're asking if I specialize in something, I'd say I do just about everything.  For instance, I used to help Sven chop lumber.
That is, until the day he almost lost his hand at the sawmill.  Wasn't my fault, he ran into me.  But he hasn't asked for my help since.
Same with Delphine. She says I broke too many dishes. I broke maybe three at the most.
Three dishes does seem like a lot. Maybe you're being too hard on her.
Ha, that woman seems sweet on the outside, but beware, she has a real mean streak too.
Gerdur though, she'll vouch for me.  And the blacksmith fellow, I forget his name.  He taught me how to strip leather down.
I'm guessing he would've hired me as his apprentice, but I think he knew I was destined for more.
I'm sensing a pattern with your previous employers.
I know what you're getting at.  I hear the whispers.  But the only pattern I see is one of versatility.
I mean I'm no fool.  Yes, I can be clumsy.  And Mara knows I'm not the best cook.
But that's only because I'm not really concentrating on what I'm doing.  And why should I?
It's not as if the lumber chopping and dish washing is a mentally exhausting skill.
I figure I can do that stuff while I fill my head with greater pursuits.
And what might those pursuits be?
The most noble pursuits that any man can endeavor.  Vanquishing vampires, beheading warlocks, and saving damsels from the claws of despair.
Whenever I work the bench, I imagine I'm hammering my foes into submission.
Whenever I deliver a letter, I imagine I'm charging the battlements of Fort Greymoor.
Sometimes when I'm in the middle of a job, I'll accidentally whisper under my breath, something like, "Die you dastardly bandit."
Oh you should see the look on my patrons' faces!  Although it's kind of like the face you're making now.
You aim to become a true hero. It is a lofty goal.
And one not easily achieved.  Which is why I have to make good use of my time.
Whenever I was tasked with doing something for the locals, I'd let my body do the work while my mind stayed focused on the art of battle.
Something on your mind?
An epic, to be precise.  One that's coming to its climax.  There's a tower on the horizon, canvassed by a sky the color of blood.
I'm the innkeeper. It's my business to keep track of strangers.
Heard any rumors lately?
Word is Ulfric Stormcloak escaped from the Imperials. War's only going to get worse, now.
Whatever you need. By Ysmir, if it's simple and strong, I can forge it.
Need any help around the forge?
Yes, actually. How about you smith me an iron dagger? Here's everything you need to make one. Go ahead.
You lookin' for a new blade?
Here's an iron dagger.
Not bad, but it's a little dull. How about you sharpen it up? Just need a bit of metal and the grindstone over there.
Iron or steel is what you need. Leave that fancy Elven stuff to the Elves.
I could forge you a warhammer that would crush a giant's head like a walnut.
Can I use your forge?
I see no harm in it, if you have the skill.
The grindstone will improve your weapons. Use the table to improve your armor.
If you've got the raw materials, you can use the forge to make something new.
Yes?
They say the College has been snooping around Saarthal. Mages in a burial crypt. No good can come of that...
May I harvest your crops?
Of course.
Think you can go blade to blade with me? You'd be dead in six seconds.
Sounds like you've got a grudge.
You been talking to those Companions?
"Too hot-headed," they cried. Weak, pathetic cowards, the lot of them!
Why'd the Companions reject you?
It wasn't my fault! I told them over and over that it was an accident!
They wanted me to prove my worth, so they threw me up against a young whelp of a lad, hardly old enough to grow his first chin hairs.
I guess they thought a woman wasn't strong enough to hurt him. I didn't mean for him to die! Why would I want that? I just... I just lost control.
You must really love to fight.
The heat of the battle is the fire that forges the strongest blades. It's an old Nord proverb.
That, and a true Nord never misses a chance to test her worth.
Got the fleetest steeds in all o' Skyrim.
Can I buy a horse?
Suppose so. Got one all saddled if you've got the coin.
On second thought, I'll walk.
Suit yourself.
Need something?
What have you got for sale?
Take a look.
Got some good pieces out here, if you're looking to buy. More inside.
What can you tell me about Whiterun?
Hmph. Plenty.
I'd say we're prosperous enough. Most folk don't go hungry, if they're willing to work hard.
The city's ruled by the Jarl up in Dragonsreach. That's the fortress, there, up on the tall hill.
But you're probably more interested in Jorrvaskr, mead hall of the Companions. Their deeds of war and valor are... legendary.
Life's hard enough with all these men propositioning me. But that bard is the worst.
Someone giving you trouble?
That bard Mikael is begging for a dagger up against his throat, the way he goes on about me.
I heard him boasting at the Bannered Mare, saying he'll "conquer me as a true Nord conquers any harsh beast." Hmph.
What if I talk to Mikael?
If you want to try, go right ahead. I don't think anything will get through that thick skull of his, though.
You get a lot of attention from men?
You've got no idea. Half the men in Whiterun have proposed to me. Some were even single.
They'll never understand. No amount of flowers or honeyed words are going to change my mind.
Right now, all that matters is my daughter Mila. No man's going to get between me and my little girl.
I'm a bard by trade. Perhaps you've heard of me?
You want a drink?
